Rashi on Yevamot 46a:10:1.english: [He] wished to immerse [him] - For the sake of Judaism, for a slave.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:10:2.english: From you I will claim him - If he precedes [you] and says [that he is immersing] for the sake of [becoming] a free man.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:10:3.english: Arvisa - [In Old French,] chevestre [a halter or bridle].

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:10:4.english: And they tightened [it] - They pressed [it] to bind [it] around his neck in order to restrain him in the water.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:10:5.hebrew: ארפו ליה וצמצמו ליה - שהיה לו עניבה, וכשרוצים מושכין ראש החבל והוא דוחק מאליו, וכשאין מושכין, רפוי, והמים נכנסים על בשרו:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:10:5.english: They loosened it and tightened it - For it had a slipknot, and when they want [to tighten it], they pull the end of the rope and it presses [tight] on its own; and when they do not pull, [it is] loose, and the water comes onto his skin.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:11:1.english: Zulta de-tina - A vessel full of clay.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:12:1.hebrew: דיהבי זוזי לאינשי לכרגייהו - כשאין נותנין כסף גולגולת למלך, תופסים אותם גבאי המלך. והני דבי פפא עשירים היו, ופורעים המס לגבאי המלך וקונין אותם לעבדים מהם. ועובדי כוכבים היו אותן הנקנין, וקא מיבעיא ליה אי הוי קנין, דלכי נפקי מיניה ליבעי גיטא דחירותא או לא:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:12:1.english: Who give money to people for their poll tax - When [people] do not pay the poll tax to the king, the king's tax-collectors seize them. And these [members] of the house of Pappa were wealthy, and they would pay the tax to the king's tax-collectors and purchase them from them as slaves. And those who were purchased were idolaters, and [Rav Pappa] asks whether it is [a valid] acquisition, such that when they go free from him, they require a bill of emancipation or not.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:13:1.english: Moharkayehu dehanei - The seal of these [people].

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:13:2.english: In the king's register - [Meaning] that they are his slaves.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:13:3.hebrew: טפסא - ארגז, אשקרי"ן בלע"ז:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:13:3.english: Tafsa - A chest, escrin in Old French.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:13:4.hebrew: ומלכא אמר כו' - הילכך, מכר הוא, ובעו גיטא דחירותא אי בעו לאיגיורי ולאשתרויי בבת ישראל:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:13:4.english: And the king says, etc. - Therefore, it is a [valid] sale, and they require a bill of emancipation if they wish to convert and become permitted to [marry] a Jewish woman.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:15:1.hebrew: לפי שאינם בני תורה - אתורמוסין קאי, דאין בו משום בישולי עובדי כוכבים כדמפרש לקמן, אלא לפי שאינן בני תורה, צא ואסור עליהן שלא יזלזלו בבשולי עובדי כוכבים:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:15:1.english: Because they are not people of Torah - [This] refers to [their] lupines, for there is no [prohibition] of food cooked by idolaters regarding them, as [the Gemara] explains below; rather, because they are not people of Torah, go and forbid [them] to them so that they will not treat food cooked by idolaters lightly.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:15:2.hebrew: ועל יינם משום יין נסך - דאע"ג דלא נגעי, אלא כחו בעלמא הוא, אסור משום "לך לך אמרין לנזירא" כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:15:2.english: And concerning their wine because of libation wine - For even though they did not touch [it], rather it is merely [their] indirect force, it is forbidden because of "Go, go, we say to the nazirite," etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:15:3.english: A lupine is not served on a king's table.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:1:1.hebrew: עובד כוכבים גופא לא קני - עובד כוכבים לא קנאו לגופו של זה מתחלה, כדאמר לקמן: "ולא הם קונים זה את זה":
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:1:1.english: A gentile does not acquire [the] body - A gentile did not acquire this [slave's] body from the outset, as [the Gemara] states below: "Nor do they acquire one another."

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:20:1.hebrew: באבותינו שמלו - בימי משה, כשיצאו ממצרים, ויצאו מכלל בני נח לקבל התורה ולקבל פני השכינה:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:20:1.english: With our forefathers who were circumcised - In the days of Moses, when they went out of Egypt, and left the category of Noahides to receive the Torah and to receive the countenance of the Divine Presence.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:20:2.hebrew: באמהות - נשותיהם שטבלו, כדמפרש לקמן; דאם לא טבלו, במה נכנסו תחת כנפי שכינה:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:20:2.english: With the foremothers - [This refers to] their wives, who immersed, as [the Gemara] explains later; for if they did not immerse, how did they enter under the wings of the Divine Presence?

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:21:1.english: From the impossible - It is impossible to circumcise [the] foremothers.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:22:1.hebrew: אלא מן החולין - ולא מדמי מעשר שני, דאכתי מעשר שני לא הוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:22:1.english: Only from non-sacred [animals] - And not from second tithe money, for second tithe did not yet exist [in Egypt].

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:22:2.english: It may be brought only from non-sacred [animals] - To exclude [purchasing it] with second tithe money.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:23:1.hebrew: ה"ג במנחות בהתודה (מנחות דף פב.), א"ל רבי עקיבא וכי דנין אפשר כו' - ומאן דגריס רבי יהושע — קשיא, האמר רבי יהושע דנין מאמהות:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:23:1.english: This is the reading in Menachot, in [the chapter] HaTodah (Menachot 82a): "Rabbi Akiva said to him: But can one derive [the] possible, etc." - And [according to] one who reads "Rabbi Yehoshua," it is difficult, for Rabbi Yehoshua said [that] we derive [the law from] the foremothers.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:23:2.hebrew: משאי אפשר - מפסח מצרים, דהאי דלא בא מן המעשר דאי אפשר הוא, דאכתי מעשר לא הוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:23:2.english: From the impossible - From the Paschal lamb of Egypt; for [the fact] that it did not come from the tithe is [a case of] "impossible," as tithe did not yet exist.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:2:1.hebrew: הקדש חמץ ושחרור - עשה שורו אפותיקי והקדישו למזבח, דהויא קדושת הגוף, פקע שיעבודא דקמא; אבל קדושת בדק הבית לא מפקעא, כדתנן בערכין (דף כג:): "מוסיף עוד דינר ופודה הנכסים כולן". או אם עשה חמצו אפותיקי לעובד כוכבים, והרי הוא מונח בידו של ישראל, ובאו שש שעות של ערב הפסח, פקע שיעבוד העובד כוכבים — הואיל ולא הוי ממש דידיה — וחייב זה לבערו:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:2:1.english: Consecration, leavened bread, and emancipation - [For example, if] one designated his ox as an apotiki [a specific mortgaged property] and consecrated it to the altar — which is intrinsic sanctity — the lien of the first [party, i.e., the creditor,] is abrogated; however, sanctity for the upkeep of the Temple does not abrogate [a lien], as we learned in a Mishnah in Arakhin (23b): "He adds another dinar and redeems all the properties." Or, if one designated his leavened bread as an apotiki for an idolater, and it is lying in the possession of the Jew, and the sixth hour of the eve of Passover arrives, the idolater's lien is abrogated — since it is not actually his — and this [Jew] is obligated to destroy it.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:2:2.hebrew: ושחרור - עשה עבדו אפותיקי לחבירו ושחררו, משוחרר, ופקע ממונו של מלוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:2:2.english: And emancipation - [If] one made his slave an apotiki [designated security] for his fellow and emancipated him, [the slave] is emancipated, and the creditor's money [i.e., lien] is abrogated.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:3:1.hebrew: בבלוריא כו' לפניה אין - לפי שהן גרים והיא עובדת כוכבים, והעובד כוכבים ישראל לא קני לגופיה:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:3:1.english: Involving Beloreya, etc.; before her — yes - Because they are converts and she is an idolater, and an idolater does not acquire the body of a Jew.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:3:2.english: After her, no - Thus, regarding a Jew, we do not say [that] a slave acquires himself [as] a freeman.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:4:1.english: Whether without a specified [intention] - That [he] did not specify, "Behold, we are immersing for the sake of [becoming] freemen."

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:4:2.hebrew: במפורש - כדרב חמא בר גוריא, דקתני וקדם וטבל לשם בן חורין:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:4:2.english: With explicit [intention] - Like [the statement of] Rav Chama bar Gurya, as it teaches: "and he went ahead and immersed for the sake of [becoming] a freeman."

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:5:1.hebrew: אבל עובד כוכבים גופיה - עובד כוכבים שמכר עצמו לישראל, קנהו ישראל לגופיה. ואם קדם וטבל לשם בן חורין, לא קנה עצמו בן חורין:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:5:1.english: But a gentile himself - [That is, a] gentile who sold himself to a Jew: the Jew has acquired him [as to] his body. And if he went ahead and immersed for the sake of [becoming] a freeman, he has not acquired himself [as] a freeman.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:7:1.hebrew: אלא עובד כוכבים מי לא קני ליה לישראל - למעשה ידיו? והכתיב: "או לעקר משפחת גר", ואמר מר: "משפחת גר" — זה העובד כוכבים:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:7:1.english: Rather, does an idolater not acquire a Jew - For his labor? Isn't it written: "or to the offshoot of a stranger's family" [Leviticus 25:47], and the Master said: "a stranger's family" — this [refers to] the idolater.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:8:1.hebrew: אימא בכספא ובטבילה - לשום עבדות הוא דקאמר רחמנא ליקני, אבל אם קדם וטבל לשם בן חורין, ה"נ דבן חורין הוא:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:8:1.english: Say with money and with immersion - It is for the sake of slavery that the Merciful One says he acquires [him], but if [the slave] went ahead and immersed for the sake of [becoming] a free man, so too [is it] that he is a free man.

Rashi on Yevamot 46a:9:1.hebrew: לתקפו במים - כשמטבילו לשם יהדות לעבדות, צריך שיתקפנו לתת עליו עול מלאכה במים, כדי שתהא נראית כטבילת עבדות, שאפילו יאמר הוא לשם בן חורין, לא קנה עצמו בן חורין, ולא יהא ממשות בדבריו:
Rashi on Yevamot 46a:9:1.english: To hold him tightly in the water - When [the master] immerses him for the sake of Judaism, for slavery, he must hold him tightly to place upon him the yoke of labor in the water, so that it appears as an immersion for slavery, so that even if [the slave] says [he is immersing] for the sake of [becoming] a free man, he has not acquired himself [as] a free man, and there will be no substance in his words.

Tosafot on Yevamot 46a:12:1.hebrew: כי נפקי צריכי גיטא דחירותא או לאו - מספקא ליה אי דינא דמלכותא דינא או לא, ואע"ג דלא קני גופיה, הכא קני, או דלמא הכא נמי לא קני אלא למעשה ידיו. ובנכריותן מיירי, אם היו באין להתגייר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 46a:12:1.english: When they go free, do they require a bill of emancipation or not - [Rav Pappa] is uncertain whether the law of the kingdom is the law [dina d'malchuta dina] or not: [whether,] even though [ordinarily] he does not acquire his body, here he does acquire [it], or perhaps here too he only acquires [him] for his handiwork. And [the Gemara] is speaking of them in their gentile state, if they were coming to convert.

Tosafot on Yevamot 46a:19:1.hebrew: רבי יוחנן כאידך לישנא ס"ל - אומר ר"ת דכולהו מודו דכשנאכל כמות שהוא חי, דאין בו משום בישולי עובדי כוכבים. דאמר באין מעמידין (ע"ז דף לח.), דאיכא בינייהו דגים קטנים, ארזי ודייסא — היינו דברים שאין עולים על שלחן מלכים ואין נאכלים כמות שהן חיין; ולא נקט כמה דברים הנאכלים כשהן חיין ועולים על שלחן מלכים, כמו פירות וגבינה וכיוצא בהן. והא דאסר רבי יוחנן התם ביצה, אע"ג דראוי לגומעה חיה — אין זו אכילה חשובה; דהכי נמי בשר מליח, מותר לטלטלו בשבת (שבת קכח.) דחזי לאכילה, ואפ"ה יש בו משום בישולי עובדי כוכבים:
Tosafot on Yevamot 46a:19:1.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan holds in accordance with the other version - Rabbeinu Tam says that all agree that when [a food] is eaten as it is raw, it is not subject to [the prohibition of] food cooked by gentiles. For that which [the Gemara] states in [the chapter] Ein Ma'amidin (Avodah Zarah 38a), that the practical difference between them is small fish, mushrooms, and porridge — these are things that do not go up on the table of kings and are not eaten as they are raw; and [the Gemara] did not mention the many things that are eaten when they are raw and go up on the table of kings, such as fruits, cheese, and the like. And as for that which Rabbi Yoḥanan prohibited an egg there, even though it is fit to be swallowed raw — that is not [considered] a significant [manner of] eating; for similarly, salted meat is permitted to be moved on Shabbat (Shabbat 128a) because it is fit for eating [raw], and even so it is subject to [the prohibition of] food cooked by gentiles.

Tosafot on Yevamot 46a:23:1.hebrew: אמר ליה ר' עקיבא וכי דנין אפשר משאי אפשר - תימה: לר' עקיבא מנלן דאין משלשין במכות? דבפרק קמא דמכות (דף ה.) ילפינן לה ממיתה, והיינו אי אפשר. ואין לומר דהתם דגזירה שוה היא מודה ר"ע דדנין משאי אפשר משום דאין ג"ש למחצה, אבל הכא בנין אב הוא — דהא הכא נמי היקישא הוא, כדמסיק בסוף התודה (מנחות דף פב: ושם), דדריש רבי אליעזר מועבדת (שמות יג) שיהו כל העבודות שוות זה כזה, ולא קיבל ר"ע, אף על גב דאין היקש נמי למחצה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 46a:23:1.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: "But can one derive the possible from the impossible?" - [This is] puzzling: according to Rabbi Akiva, from where do we [know] that we do not divide lashes into thirds? For in the first chapter of Makkot (5a) we derive it from [the] death [penalty], and that is [deriving from the] impossible! And one cannot say that there, since it is a gezeirah shavah, Rabbi Akiva concedes that we derive [the possible] from the impossible because there is no partial gezeirah shavah, whereas here it is a binyan av — for here too it is a hekesh, as [the Gemara] concludes at the end of [the chapter] HaTodah (Menachot 82b, and there [elsewhere]), where Rabbi Eliezer expounds from "ve'avadta" ["And you shall perform this service"] (Exodus 13) that all services should be equal to one another, and Rabbi Akiva did not accept [it], even though there is also no partial hekesh.

Tosafot on Yevamot 46a:2:1.english: Consecration, leavened bread, and emancipation - [This] is explained in [the chapter entitled] HaSholeach (Gittin 40b):
